NEW DELHI: BJP MP Kangana Ranaut on Wednesday launched a sharp attack on Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi over the continuing stalemate in Parliament, accusing him of making a "mockery" of the House and the country while refusing the government's offer for a debate on the students' protest.Ranaut alleged that Gandhi was demanding a statement from Union home minister Amit Shah over the police action against protesters, while simultaneously saying the opposition would not listen to him."I feel he is making a mockery of the country. He constantly ridicules the nation; for him, everything is a joke. This is the first time I am seeing Parliament being made such a mockery of. In the same breath, he says, 'We want an answer from Amit Shah ji--asking whether or not he did such-and-such to the students--while simultaneously declaring, 'We are not here to listen to him'. He has no sense of shame or propriety left," news agency ANI quoted Ranaut saying."The whole world is watching and wondering what kind of person this is. The way he is venting his frustration and insulting Parliament and, by extension, the entire nation and its citizens convinces me, as someone observing his role as leader of the opposition, that this will be his final term," she added.Ranaut, who represents Mandi in the Lok Sabha, also attacked Gandhi over his political record, saying the Congress under his leadership had "lost a hundred elections" and claiming that he would not retain the leader of opposition post in the future."He is demanding the resignation of the Prime Minister--a democratically elected leader who has secured a massive mandate for a third consecutive term. He seems to think that no one else in this country should even exist but him. Then there are his other actions--colluding with figures like Soros or international forces to tear the country apart and leave it in ruins. Ultimately, it doesn't matter whose resignation he demands or what he wants, because the public simply doesn't care about him," she said.The BJP MP's remarks came amid a continuing face-off between the government and the opposition over the July 20 student protests in Delhi. Opposition parties have been demanding a statement from Amit Shah over the alleged police action against protesters, leading to repeated adjournments. The Monsoon Session is set to end on Thursday.
Article Summary: BJP MP Kangana Ranaut accuses Rahul Gandhi of making a "mockery" of the House and the country. Gandhi is demanding a statement from Union home minister Amit Shah over the police action against protesters, while simultaneously saying the opposition would not listen to him. The Monsoon Session is set to end on Thursday.

Article Title: 'Acting like goondas': CJP’s Saurav Das claims Pondicherry Police ‘harassed’ kin, claims Centre link
Article Text:
CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das claims police action at his home in Puducherry

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das on Wednesday alleged that Puducherry Police officials visited his family home and subjected his family members to questioning, claiming that the action was aimed at intimidating him into silence.In a post on X, Das said police officials arrived at his family’s residence around two hours before his post and questioned his family members.“Why this harassment, Puducherry Police? Who ordered this and for what purpose? Is this the legal procedure?” Das asked.He further alleged that the BJP government in Puducherry was attempting to intimidate his family and claimed that the action was being carried out at the behest of the Union government.Das questioned whether visiting his family home and questioning his relatives was part of the legal procedure, and sought clarity on the reasons behind the police action.“If the intention is to intimidate me into silence, it will not work,” Das said, adding that the incident would instead strengthen his resolve to push for what he described as a better system in which police “uphold the law”.Das also accused the police of acting like “goondas” and said the alleged action was inconsistent with the character of the Puducherry government.Reacting to the same, TMC MP Mahua Moitra in an X post wrote, "Welcome to BJP land Dear…. where police belongs to the 2 Bhais.."

Das claims action was aimed at intimidating him into silence. TMC MP Mahua Moitra in an X post wrote, "Welcome to BJP land Dear…. where police belongs to the 2 Bhais.."
